0.1.0.en: First draft version, basic on and off capabilities and running console app detection with flow cards. Support a nice discovery functionality that requires no input from the user.

0.3.0.en: Added support for buttons and media controls, if you authorize the app you get app artwork and nice names in the media screen. Added workflow support to send buttons to the console.

0.3.1.en: Updated to 0.6.4 of package xbox-smartglass to improve stability and fixed nexus button not working

0.5.4.en: Addd support for hew device class gameconsole

0.6.0.en: Stability: catch malformed packets from the console so the app no longer crashes. Fast button presses: await channel-ready instead of a fixed 25s wait. Lazy session management: no persistent SmartGlass session by default, so the console can stay in low-power / silent install mode. New device setting 'Track active app' (opt-in) for users who need the 'app playing changed' and 'started gaming' flow triggers.

0.7.0.en: Microsoft sign-in: new 'Sign in with Microsoft' button in the app settings replaces the copy-paste-the-token flow. The browser opens, you sign in, you're done. Two-factor accounts work. Advanced section keeps a paste-the-redirect-URL fallback for environments where the redirect can't reach Homey. Token plumbing is cleaner and refresh handling is more reliable.

0.7.1.en: Adds the community forum topic and source repository so the Homey app store links the right places for support and code.

0.7.2.en: Fix: 'Track active app' now defaults to on. The previous default suppressed 'app playing changed' and 'started gaming' triggers and delayed album art until the user pressed a button. A SmartGlass session by itself does not wake the console — only adding the input control does — so keeping the session open is safe. Existing devices are migrated automatically. The first controller button after a long idle is also faster because the session is already open.

0.7.3.en: Faster first controller button: replaces the channel-open path that waited for the next console_status (which can take 30s) with a direct start_channel_request that fires immediately. Console-rejected opens now surface as a real error. Power off command now sends the shutdown packet three times in quick succession so a single dropped UDP datagram no longer silently no-ops the off action. Added structured logging around channel open and power off so failures are diagnosable from the Homey app log.

0.7.4.en: Fix: the very first controller button after a channel was opened often got dropped because the Xbox needs ~250ms after start_channel_response to finish binding its input handler. We now send a no-op gamepad packet right after the channel opens to prime the binding, so the user's actual button press lands on an already-bound channel.

0.7.5.en: Fix: power off now actually works. The SmartGlass session is upgraded from anonymous to authenticated when you are signed in via 'Sign in with Microsoft' in the app settings — passing the Xbox Live user hash and XSTS token to the connect. The console silently ignores power_off from anonymous sessions, which is why earlier attempts went nowhere. If you are not signed in the session stays anonymous and buttons / media still work, but power off won't.

0.7.6.en: Surface album art / game art failures in the app log. Two silent .catch(()=>{}) blocks were hiding titlehub auth issues, CDN failures and image-update errors, making missing artwork undiagnosable. Every step of the active-app detection pipeline now logs the AUM ID, titlehub response, image URL and fetch result so the cause of a blank cover shows up directly in the Homey app log.

0.7.7.en: Fix: Microsoft sign-in now persists across app restarts. The previous OAuth scope used 'XboxLive.offline_access' which Microsoft did not honor, so MS returned an access token but no refresh token — the sign-in appeared successful but album art and power-off stopped working as soon as the access token expired. Now uses the standard 'offline_access' scope, which returns a proper refresh token. After updating: open the app settings and click 'Sign in with Microsoft' once more. Also cleans up some stray 'undefined' log lines from flow-trigger handlers.

0.7.8.en: Several reliability fixes for setups with multiple consoles. Refresh-token rotation is now serialized so multiple devices starting up in parallel no longer hit the Microsoft token endpoint N times in a row. Session opening is also serialized so concurrent _ensureSession calls share one connect attempt — duplicate session-established lines are gone. Malformed-packet warnings from the underlying library (seen on Series X firmware) are throttled to one warning per minute with a count of suppressed duplicates, so the Homey app log stays readable.

1.0.0.en: First stable release. Highlights since the previous public version: one-click Sign in with Microsoft (no more copy-pasting a token), persistent sign-in across restarts, current game and box art shown on the device tile, fast and reliable controller buttons (first press now lands in under a second), no longer keeps the console awake during silent installs, and the app no longer crashes on packets from newer Xbox firmware. Known limitation: turning the console off is not supported on Xbox Series X / S — Microsoft moved that to a cloud channel that this app does not use. Power off still works on the original Xbox One.

1.1.0.en: Two cloud-powered additions, both unlocked by Microsoft sign-in. The 'Launch an app or game' flow action finally works, with a live dropdown of what is actually installed on the selected console — no more guessing AUM IDs. And turning a Series X / S off now goes through the same cloud channel the official Xbox phone app uses, so it actually shuts the console down. Local-first behaviour is preserved: nothing new runs in the background, sign-in is still optional, and Xbox One keeps using the local network for power off.

1.2.0.en: Optional Xbox Live profile tracking. Enable 'Track Xbox Live profile' in the app settings to add a Gamerscore tile to your Xbox devices and unlock two new flow triggers: 'Achievement unlocked' (fires when you earn an achievement, with tokens for the game, the achievement name, gamerscore awarded and art) and 'Friend came online' (fires when one of your Xbox Live friends transitions to online, with their gamertag and current game as tokens). This adds about one Xbox Live API call per minute when enabled. Off by default. Also: power-on now falls back to the cloud WakeUp command if the local magic packet doesn't reach the console (useful when the console moved to a different IP or sits behind a VLAN), provided you are signed in.

1.2.1.en: The 'Achievement unlocked' and 'Friend came online' flow triggers now also carry binary image tokens — the achievement artwork and the friend's gamerpic — alongside the existing URL tokens. Drop them straight into a notification, push, or Telegram action without having to fetch the URL yourself.

1.2.2.en: Two friend-presence fixes. The trigger no longer fires repeatedly while a friend bounces between Online and Away/Idle states — anything that isn't explicitly offline now counts as present, so one transition fires once. And the 'Game they're playing' token is no longer blank: the presenceDetails entries from Microsoft's peoplehub use PascalCase field names and we now read those correctly, plus we prefer the entry actually flagged as a game over arbitrary list order.

1.2.3.en: New flow trigger 'Friend went offline' — fires when one of your Xbox Live friends transitions from online to offline. Includes a 'Last game they were playing' token so you know what they were doing just before they signed off, alongside the same gamertag, display name and gamerpic (URL + binary) tokens as the came-online trigger.

1.2.4.en: Two new filtered flow triggers: 'A specific friend came online' and 'A specific friend went offline'. Pick the friend from a searchable dropdown — the flow only fires for that one person, so you can build 'when [partner] comes online, do X' without a When-card with an If-check. Same tokens as the generic friend triggers (gamertag, display name, game, gamerpic URL + binary). The generic 'Friend came online' / 'Friend went offline' triggers are unchanged.

1.2.5.en: Three new flow condition cards for use in the 'And' column. 'A specific friend is online' checks a single friend (with the same searchable dropdown as the triggers). 'A specific friend is playing a game' matches when the cached game title contains the text you provide (case-insensitive, so 'Halo' matches 'Halo Infinite'). 'Any Xbox Live friend is online' is true when at least one friend is online. All three are evaluated against the presence cache the background poller refreshes about once a minute, so no extra API calls are made when a flow runs.

1.2.6.en: New 'Event log' panel in the app settings, visible when signed in. Shows the last 200 interesting Xbox Live events the background poller has captured: achievements unlocked, friends coming online or going offline (including which game they were playing), and any fetch failures. Persists across restarts so you can check hours later. Also broadens how the friend's current game is detected — peoplehub uses different field names per title, so the previous extractor sometimes returned an empty game. It now tries TitleName, RichPresence and PresenceText, with a top-level fallback for cases where the title only lives there.

1.2.7.en: Two new flow triggers for the case where a friend who is already online switches from one game to another (a thing the event log surfaced but flows couldn't react to). 'Friend switched game' fires for any friend; 'A specific friend switched game' filters on the friend you pick from the dropdown. Tokens include both the previous and the new game name, plus the usual gamertag, display name and gamerpic (URL + binary). Only fires when both titles are real games — going from no-game to a game (or back) is already covered by the came-online trigger.

1.2.8.en: Sign-in is now much harder to lose. Previous versions wiped the Microsoft refresh token the very first time Microsoft returned 'invalid_grant', which sometimes triggered on transient hiccups at app start. Now the app keeps a backup of the previous refresh token across one rotation and tries that first; only after three consecutive real failures is the token actually wiped. Network errors and 5xx responses never count as failures. Every refresh, rotation, fallback or wipe is also written to the event log so you can see exactly what's happening. The settings page now shows 'Token last rotated: …' under the signed-in status so you can spot when rotations stop happening.

1.2.9.en: When the Microsoft refresh token does expire and gets wiped (after the three-strike defensive logic added in 1.2.8 gives up), the app now posts a Homey notification asking you to re-sign-in. Previously you only saw it in the event-log panel, which is fine for diagnostics but not great if you're not looking. The notification links to the app via the standard 'open app' path; tap the Xbox console companion entry and the settings page opens where you can sign in again.

1.3.0.en: Microsoft refresh tokens now last weeks instead of about a day. Previous releases used an SPA-style sign-in, which Microsoft caps to a 24-hour refresh-token lifetime as a security measure for single-page apps. The token-exchange path has been switched to the public Mobile/Desktop platform, which gives a 90-day sliding-window refresh token. One-time action required: open the app settings, tap 'Sign out', then tap 'Sign in with Microsoft' again. After that you should not see the periodic 're-authorization required' notification anymore.

1.3.1.en: Fixes the 'Achievement unlocked' flow trigger silently missing real unlocks. The Microsoft achievement query used a wrong orderBy value and a server-side filter parameter that has had inconsistent names across releases, which let locked achievements slip into the seen-set and made later unlocks look already-seen. The query now uses orderBy=UnlockTime and filters on progressState in code, which is authoritative. The list of recent titles checked grows from 5 to 10, and the seen-set is automatically wiped once on upgrade so the next first tick re-seeds with the corrected data. The seed entry in the event-log now also shows the most-recently-unlocked achievement found (title + name + timestamp), so you can verify the pipeline reaches the right data. Top-level failures of the achievements / friends / gamerscore tick now also write to the event log instead of only the developer console.

1.3.2.en: Follow-up to the 1.3.1 achievement fix: the previous endpoint we used to find recently-played games (achievements.xboxlive.com /history/titles) turned out not to sort by recency at all, so freshly-played games could fall out of the window while old ones from years ago stayed in. Switched to titlehub /titleHistory, which is sorted by last-played descending and is the same data the official Xbox app uses. The seen-set is automatically wiped again on upgrade so the next first tick re-seeds against the right games — you should see a much more recent 'most recent' entry in the event log.
